why_angle: The cited Minn Kota pages give breaker sizes and say to 'verify enough continuous amperage', but none of them checks a named battery's continuous rating against the 60 A a QUEST motor draws. None of them says that Minn Kota's onboard chargers can't charge a single 24V or 36V lithium battery either; that page appeared only as an uncited result. So the single 24V/36V battery the rivals preferred came with no matching charger. This page puts the right charger in the cart, rules out a 50 A-BMS 36V pack for QUEST and 112 lb motors, and gives the headroom arithmetic for each kit.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Current headroom. 24V kits: 100 A − 60 A QUEST max = 40 A spare. 12V kit: 120 A − 50 A (55 lb 12V max) = 70 A spare. Redodo 36V 50Ah on a 36V QUEST: 50 A − 60 A = 10 A short.
  • Refill time. 24V 100Ah on a 20 A charger: 100 Ah ÷ 20 A = 5 h. 12V 120Ah on a 20 A charger: 120 Ah ÷ 20 A = 6 h. A 12V 100Ah lithium on one 10 A bank of a Minn Kota MK 330PCL: 100 Ah ÷ 10 A = 10 h.
  • Full-throttle runtime. 24V 100Ah at 60 A: 100 Ah ÷ 60 A = 1.7 h. Redodo 36V 50Ah at 60 A: 50 Ah ÷ 60 A = 0.83 h, and its BMS allows 60 A for 30 minutes at most.
  • Cost per watt-hour. 24V kit: $579.98 ÷ 2,560 Wh = $0.23/Wh. Group 31 bundle: $674.48 ÷ 2,560 Wh = $0.26/Wh. 12V kit: $379.98 ÷ 1,536 Wh = $0.25/Wh.
  • What the compact case costs. $674.48 − $579.98 = $94.50 extra for the Group 31 size and Bluetooth.

Most bass boats run a 24V motor, and the cheapest complete 24V cart is the one-battery kit: Redodo's 24V 100Ah with the 29.2V 20A charger, $579.98 together. {kit:kit-24v-one-battery}

If your tray is Group 31 size and space is tight, Redodo sells its smaller 24V 100Ah with a 24V 20A charger as one SKU. Measure first: Redodo says it fits Group 31 trays but not standard Group 31 battery boxes. {kit:kit-24v-group-31-tray}

For a 12V motor, the 120Ah Group 24 battery drops into Group 24, 27 or 31 boxes, and its 120 A rating leaves wide headroom. If your boat already has a Minn Kota PCL charger, it can charge a 12V LiFePO4 battery, so you can skip the charger in this cart. {kit:kit-12v-kayak-jon-boat}

The charger and the 60 A check

Charger. Minn Kota states that its chargers 'are not compatible with single 24V and 36V Lithium Batteries' and that they 'are designed for 12 Volt battery systems only'. Each bank charges one 12V battery, and batteries wired in series can't be charged on one bank. If you keep two or three 12V batteries in series, a Minn Kota multi-bank charger still works, one bank per battery. Its maximum is 14.5 V, so check that against the battery maker's charge voltage. If you switch to one 24V or 36V lithium battery, you also need a 29.2 V or 43.8 V LiFePO4 charger. That's why each 24V kit above includes one.

Current. Minn Kota says QUEST motors 'are designed to not pull more than 60 amps on high speed' and that breakers larger than 60 A should not be used on them. It also says a lithium battery without enough continuous current shows up as a motor that runs for a short time and then shuts off. The battery's continuous rating, not its peak, has to cover the motor's max draw. Put a 60 A breaker such as Minn Kota's MKR-27 between the battery and the motor. Redodo doesn't sell one, so buy it separately.

For a 36V QUEST or a 112 lb motor, Redodo sells no single 36V battery rated for 60 A continuous. The practical route is three 12V lithium batteries in series on a 3-bank charger, one bank per battery. Before you buy, check that each battery's continuous rating covers the motor's max draw and that its maker allows series wiring.

Not recommended

Redodo 36V 50Ah on a 36V QUEST or a 112 lb motor. Redodo markets it for 100–120 lb motors, but rates it at 50 A continuous and 60 A for up to 30 minutes. That is below the 60 A a QUEST can pull and the 52 A Minn Kota lists for a 112 lb motor, so hard Spot-Lock or full throttle can trip the BMS. It suits a 101 lb, 46 A motor.
